# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 76 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 76 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_076_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Part 3 — The Rejected Stones and the Virgins

**76:1** Some stones were brought from the deep and placed in the building, and they joined well with the stones already set in from the plain — for they were very bright. But some of these were brought by men and did not fit into the building; these were set aside near the tower, because they could not be used in the structure. For they had not received the seal, while the others all had the seal of the virgins.

**76:2** "Who are these virgins?" I asked the shepherd. "They are holy spirits," he said. "And a man cannot enter the kingdom of God in any other way unless these clothe him with their garment. For if you receive the name but do not receive the garment from them, it profits you nothing. For these virgins are the Powers of the Son of God. If you bear the name but do not bear his power, you will carry his name in vain."

**76:3** "But the stones that were rejected — who are they?" I said. "These," he said, "are those who bore the name but did not put on the garment of the virgins." "And what is their garment, lord?" I said. "The names themselves are the garment," he said. "Everyone who bears the name of the Son of God ought also to bear the names of these virgins. For the Son of God himself bears the names of these virgins."

**76:4** "But those stones that were thrown far from the tower and fell onto the road and then rolled off the road into the rough terrain — who are they?" "These," he said, "are those who had believed, but then because of their double-mindedness abandoned the true road. Thinking they could find a better road, they went astray and were afflicted, wandering over the rough places."

**76:5** "And those that fell into the fire and were burned — who are they?" "These," he said, "are those who fully apostatized from the living God, and repentance no longer entered their hearts, because of the desires of their licentiousness and the wicked deeds which they committed."

**76:6** "And who are those that fell near the waters and could not roll into the water?" "These," he said, "are those who heard the word and wished to be baptized in the name of the Lord. But then, when the purity of the truth came to their memory, they drew back and went off again after their evil desires."

---

*LOGOS renders according to the Greek text of P.Mich. 130 with attention to the allegorical typology of rejected stones and the virgins-as-Powers christology of Similitude 9.*
